title: Clique interdiction
description: Delete at most k nodes of a graph so that no clique of c nodes is left; with k and c in the input this is Sigma-2-complete (Rutenburg). The check finds a surviving clique and the refinement says that one of its nodes has to be deleted; the loop takes up to three cliques per candidate. Try n = 17 with k = 9 (51 solutions).

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The graph. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% The Paley graph on n nodes (n a prime of the form 4m + 1): two nodes are joined when
% their difference is a square modulo n.
node(0..n-1).
square((X*X) \ n) :- X = 1..n-1.
edge(U,V) :- node(U), node(V), U < V, square((V-U) \ n).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): at most k deleted nodes.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: at most k nodes to delete.
{ del(V) : node(V) } k.
#show del/1.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the deleted nodes.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for a clique of c nodes that survives (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: c nodes that are not deleted and pairwise joined.
c { q(V) : node(V) } c.
:- q(V), del(V).
:- q(U), q(V), U < V, not edge(U,V).
#show q/1.

% The clique survives as long as none of its nodes is deleted.
relevant(del(V)) :- q(V).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Up to three surviving cliques per candidate; each gives one clause
# ("delete one of these nodes"). The candidate is rejected once.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        for X in C.models(assume G(M), limit 3):
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

instances.facts: % The Paley graph on 13 nodes with only 5 deletions: some triangle always survives, no solution.
% The 5-cycle (Paley graph on 5 nodes) with c = 2: delete a vertex cover of at most 3 nodes.
% The Paley graph on 17 nodes, 9 deletions (the guide quotes this count).
% The Paley graph on 13 nodes with up to 7 deletions.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)

solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        for X in C.models(assume G(M), limit 0):
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    L = C.models(assume G(M), limit 3)
    if L.size == 0:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))
    for X in L:
        A.add(G.clause(M, X))

solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
